sanskrit: dhanyāḥ sarasvatī skando jinaś ca jagati trayaḥ / paṭāntalagnatṛṇavatkṣipto vyādhūya yaiḥ smaraḥ // marubhūtau vadatyevamudvignaṃ vīkṣya gomukham / naravāhanadattas taṃ samarthayitum abhyadhāt // vinodanārthametanme gomukho yuktamuktavān / snigdho hi virahāyāse sādhuvādaṃ dadāti kim // samāśvāso yathāśakti svajanair virahāturaḥ / ataḥ paraṃ sa jānāti devaścāsamasāyakaḥ // ityādi jalpañ chṛṇvaṃś ca tāstāḥ parijanātkathāḥ / naravāhanadattas tāṃ triyāmāmatyavāhayat //
english: Happy in the world are Sarasvatī, Skanda and Buddha, these three who have brushed off and flung away love, like a blade of grass clinging to the skirt of the robe.” When Marubhūti said this, Naravāhanadatta, perceiving that Gomukha was distressed, said in order to comfort him: “What Gomukha said to me was appropriate, and it was said to amuse me, for what loving friend exults over one in the agony of separation? One afflicted by the pain of separation should be comforted by his friends to the best of their ability, and the sequel should be left to the disposal of the five-arrowed god.” Talking in this style, and hearing various tales from his attendants, Naravāhanadatta somehow managed to get through that night.
